Active mitoses and disrupted architecture without normal ducts or lobules are evident. Stromal infiltration by atypical cells supports malignancy, consistent with breast carcinoma characteristics. evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma histology
evidence.text: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma can show lepidic, acinar, papillary, micropapillary, or solid growth with mucin, and mixed patterns are common. Squamous differentiation is supported morphologically by keratinization, keratin pearl formation, and intercellular bridges. Poorly differentiated tumors may require immunohistochemistry.

review.assessment: The vision models consistently misclassified the case as lung squamous cell carcinoma or other non-breast malignancies, contradicting the explicit pathology report.
rationale: The de-identified report explicitly describes breast tissue with pleomorphic cells, disrupted ductal architecture, and stromal infiltration consistent with breast carcinoma.
The report's description of 'disrupted architecture without normal ducts or lobules' aligns with the case-specific prompt for breast invasive carcinoma.

Retrieved literature on lung and colorectal morphology [PMC:4367552-LungMorphology, PMC:3418538-ColorectalMorphology] describes features (keratin pearls, dirty necrosis) not mentioned in the case report.
discrepancies: All four vision models (CONCH, MUSK, PLIP, QUILTNET) failed to identify the breast origin, with a strong bias toward lung squamous cell carcinoma.
recommended_review: Pathologist review of the original slides to confirm the breast origin and evaluate the grade of the invasive carcinoma.
limitations: The assessment relies heavily on the provided text report as the vision models showed poor alignment with the ground truth.
